final_message:
The strategy is done and `report.json` is written. All 27 training instances give a certified value above the Bernoulli lower wall, and no search I ran found a better law.

**Structure:** the best law has atoms {0, a, 1}, with a = (t − l)/k. The free weight on a is found by a 200-point grid followed by golden-section refinement. In 26 of the 27 instances one end weight goes to zero, so the law has only 2 atoms: {a, 1} or {0, a}.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| 4-atom pass {0, a, b, 1}, b from j·a + k·b + l = t | Never better (float ties only) |
| Free random search, 2–5 atoms, on the 27 training instances | Never better |
| Same search on 16 new random instances, n = 3–8 | Never better |
| Run time per call | ≤ 3.1 s (n = 6), with a 3.5 s cutoff on the search |

**Departure from the hypothesis:** the conjecture says l + k ≤ n − 1, but some optima need k = n. For example, n3_m1-5_t3-20 uses a = t/3. The search therefore uses all k ≤ n and l < n.

**Confidence rule** (all training instances get 0.8):

| n | Confidence |
|---|---|
| ≤ 2 (solved cases) | 0.9 |
| 3–6 | 0.8 |
| 7–8 | 0.7 |
| 9–12 | 0.55 |
| > 12 | 0.4 |

If the 4-atom pass hits the time limit, the value goes down by 0.15.

**Not settled:**
- There is no proof that this law is optimal for n ≥ 3.
- The random search is local, so it can miss a narrow better law.
- I did not test n > 8 against an independent search.

I deleted my temporary exploration scripts. `strategy.py` has the 5-line header that the task asks for.
